comment.body:
Excellent disambiguation.

The air that Peterson's bullshit floats on is behaviorism. Behaviorally you can't tell the difference, because you're looking at it from the outside. Spiritually -- intent, motivation, purpose, essence that you can feel -- they're not only opposite, they are as far as east from west. Not just opposite in nature and function, but originating from deathly opposed forces -- irreconcilable, antagonistic spirits.

Jesus said, "Stop judging by mere appearances, but instead judge correctly."

That's right, all you "Judge NOT!" thought-terminated cultists, you are supposed to judge -- you just have no freaking clue how.

Don't just look at what you see, and don't just look at who or what they got it from -- that's just passing the buck --  look at what it actually is, what motivated it to become, what it's intent on doing, and what it defines as success. And pay attention to how it feels, because all the other considerations begin there, anyway. 

Regardless of the BS and adware, people are intent on doing what they actually do, systems do what they were designed to do, and the results in fact achieved are exactly what they wanted, otherwise they'd have done something different. At the very least, they won't keep on doing it while burying you with tomes that explain why it's the only thing that can be done and anything else would be worse.

Insanity isn't only doing the same proven-to-fail nonsense while hoping for a different result.

Insanity is also to let people that claim they're picking apples bloody your nose over and over, while you fuck your own mind over contorting everything to make it come out true.

Not only do you, as a matter of fact, believe liars -- you were trained to prefer believing them. That was the mindfuck. That's what needs to be fixed.

comment.name: Millard J Melnyk
comment.body:
Bottom line, even anarchists are authority addicts. Codependents, in other words. 

The secret/hidden premise underlying all philosophy -- anarchistic or otherwise -- is that the human psyche, when left to its own devices, will fail—so, we need some systematic rationalization that can be instituted as authoritative. 

Many opt for "natural law" -- not because it makes a lick of sense, but because most of us simply cannot think outside the paradigm of rules that compel.

Since everyone demands rules, here are four that, were they adhered to, would realize every good thing any anarchist has aspired to:



1. Be honest. Uncomfortably honest. Daringly honest. Painfully honest.

2. Absolutely refuse to tolerate or accept anything less than peerness.

3. Prioritize – absolutely – people over "property", or even more to the point, persons over shit.

4. Logically and psychologically entailed by the other pillars, insist on a completely free flow of information.

Those rules are not philosophical. They're not religious. They're not even "moral". 

They're just what we'd naturally do if we hadn't been mindfucked. They're what we naturally do with people we truly care about. They're natural and fundamental to humanness. 

And they absolutely block inhumanness.

I've read philosophy and anarchist thought since college in the 70s. I've never understood why these issues were made so complicated. 

They're not complicated.

Now I see the reason: codependence -- the addiction to authority.

Even anarchists haven’t kicked the habit.
